growth_story.headline: Cyprus fell hard when its oversized banks failed in 2013, then grew fast on services exports; income per person reached a new high in 2025.
growth_story.arc: From 1990 to 2006 income per person grew 2.9 percent a year, and the IMF describes money from abroad, drawn by low company taxes, swelling the banks and feeding a credit and housing boom before the global financial crisis. From 2007 to 2014 growth averaged -2.0 percent a year: the banks were heavily exposed to Greece, and Greek debt losses plus a falling housing market led to the 2013 banking crisis, when the two largest banks were resolved and uninsured depositors took losses. Income per person fell from 27,449 constant dollars in 2008 to 22,374 in 2014. From 2015 to 2025 growth averaged 3.8 percent a year (3.9 over 2016 to 2025, after -1.0 in the decade before), with a pandemic drop of -4.5 in 2020 and a rebound of 9.7 in 2021. The IMF credits strong domestic demand and services exports, above all ICT and tourism, helped by foreign companies moving to Cyprus from 2022. Income per person passed its 2008 level in 2019 and reached a new high of 33,527 in 2025, though yearly growth has slowed to 1.6 in 2023 and 2.3 in both 2024 and 2025.

threads.title: Foreign money builds a boom
threads.text: Before the 2008 crisis, money from abroad, drawn by low company taxes, poured into Cypriot banks. It paid for fast lending and a housing boom, and the banks grew far larger than the economy around them.

citations.title: Cyprus: Request for Arrangement under the Extended Fund Facility (IMF Country Report No. 13/125)
citations.quote: Sizeable non-resident inflows attracted by the low corporate tax regime led to a rapid increase in the size of the banking sector

threads.title: Greek losses and a bank collapse
threads.text: Cypriot banks lent heavily in Greece and held Greek government bonds. When Greece restructured its debt and Cypriot house prices fell, the two largest banks were found insolvent, and in 2013 they were resolved with losses for uninsured depositors. Income per person fell every year from 2009 to 2014.

threads.title: A slow cleanup of crisis debts
threads.text: Bad loans left over from the crisis keep falling but remain high, and many have moved out of the banks. Bank credit to the private sector shrank from 254.7 percent of GDP in 2013 to 56.7 in 2024, so the recent growth has come with much less bank credit relative to the size of the economy.

threads.title: From Russian links to ICT hub
threads.text: Cyprus used to earn much from financial and professional services tied to Russia. From 2022, foreign companies moved to Cyprus and ICT and business services grew. The IMF now names ICT and tourism as the leading services exports behind growth.

growth_story.tension: The IMF calls Cyprus's recent growth among the highest in the EU, but in the data income per person grew only 1.6 percent in 2023 and 2.3 in 2024 and 2025, far below the 6.7 of 2022 and 9.7 of 2021. Part of the gap may be that more people are sharing the output: the IMF describes foreign companies and their staff moving to Cyprus, which can lift total output faster than income per person.
